title: syntax-count
summary: Counts modern syntax in the parse of every unit, uncapped: Delphi 13 if-expressions, is not, not in; inline var/const; anonymous methods; multiline strings
intro: Read this when you want to know how much of a codebase uses a given syntax feature -- for example how many Delphi 13 if-expressions or is-not tests a downgrade would have to rewrite. It parses each unit at the call and counts shapes in the parse, so strings and comments never count and nothing is capped.

help: counts syntax features in the tree-sitter parse of each unit -- shapes, not text, so strings
and comments never count; uncapped. Features: if-expr, is-not, not-in (Delphi 13), inline-var,
inline-const (10.3), anon-method (2009), multiline-string (12); --feature picks some (default all).
--db = every .pas/.dpr/.dpk/.inc row of that index (opened read-only, nothing written);
--in adds a path (repeatable). Text as written: no $IFDEF evaluation, every branch counts.
--per-file lists files with a hit; --hits lists path:line:col per occurrence.
json: features[], files_scanned, files_unreadable, files_with_parse_errors, totals{feature: n},
files[{path, counts}] (--per-file), hits[{feature, path, line, col}] (--hits).
Exit 0 = counted (zero included); 2 = no --db/--in, unknown --feature, unreadable index;

questions.ask: How many Delphi 13 if-expressions and is-not tests does this project use?
Where exactly is each is-not test?
Which units use inline variables, and how many each?
